messages:
Lee (eng-security): Heads-up — we plan to roll a VPC egress-tightening policy in us-west-2 tomorrow 09:00 UTC. In staging the policy caused KMS grant shadowing for the ephemeral role used by GPU node bootstrap. Several nodes got stuck in \"locking\" during bootstrap because the keystore proxy saw STS:GetCallerIdentity denies. Need mitigation suggestions.

Maya (eng-platform): ugh. can we make a short-lived exception for the keystore-proxy CIDRs so bootstrap traffic isn't blocked?

Ashok (eng-infra): we repro'd this in staging earlier today — when logshipper sampling spiked it saturated NAT conntrack, which delayed egress for the keystore path and made it look like an auth failure. two different failure modes colliding.

Jordan (eng-sre): proposed quick plan: 1) temp allowlist for keystore-proxy to bypass the new deny 2) lower logshipper sampling to previous qc level (runtime flag) 3) schedule conntrack bump on the canaries. Which of 1-3 is fastest?

Lee (eng-security): allowlist is fastest. but note the policy change also dropped sts:TagSession for the ephemeral roles — that removal is why some KMS grants failed even when network allowed traffic.

Maya (eng-platform): can we patch the IAM policy to preserve TagSession for service roles only? pinging @security-policy for a quick review.

Lee (eng-security): minimal IAM diff we validated in staging (keeps TagSession for privileged service roles):

```
- "Action": ["sts:TagSession"],
- "Resource": "*",
- "Effect": "Deny",
+ (keep sts:TagSession for arn:aws:iam::*:role/redwood-service/*)
```

Ashok (eng-infra): conntrack increase needs infra deploy (kube-proxy config + host sysctl), ~20m and a short rolling restart of the warm-pool agents. rate-limiting logshipper is immediate via config.

Jordan (eng-sre): cost/ops note — if we short-circuit keystore traffic onto privatelink endpoints we avoid NAT egress and conntrack pressure but we add privatelink endpoint costs (~$0.01/hr each + data processing). Might be cheaper at scale but not for short-term canary.

Maya (eng-platform): agreed. short-term recipe: 1) apply keystore-proxy allowlist in us-west-2 2) patch IAM to retain TagSession for redwood-service roles 3) throttle logshipper sampling to previous rate 4) schedule conntrack bump during 02:00-03:00 UTC low window and do a canary in eu-west-1 first. I'll own coordination.

Lee (eng-security): sounds good. I'm tagging @oncall-sre-bot and @deploy-bot. Doing the allowlist change now (will post delta).

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: firewall/egress-policy/usw2 allowlist -> canary -> rollout (triggered by Lee). ETA 5m.

oncall-sre-bot: Noted. I'll watch warm-pool health and escalate on >5min bootstrap failures.

Ashok (eng-infra): once allowlist is up I'll push the logshipper rate change (runtime). then schedule conntrack bump for the 02:00 window.

Maya (eng-platform): thanks — will confirm canary results in this thread. :thumbsup:

Lee (eng-security): confirmed allowlist applied to canary cluster (usw2-canary). early metrics show KMS auth success rate back to normal and GPU bootstrap moving to ready state. Monitoring for 15m.

Maya (eng-platform): canary passed at +12m. proceeding to roll out the IAM patch and logshipper throttle to staging, then prod after 30m observation.

Lee (eng-security): thanks everyone. follow-up doc: I'll open a short postmortem-style note in #eng-platform with root cause and long-term mitigations (privatelink path + better conntrack autoscaling).
